description: Designing an interactive explorable map of Mars with objectives.
summary: Jezero Marswalk is a walkable first-person 3D map of part of Jezero Crater, built from NASA Mars Trek terrain and imagery. The timeline is set to future where a Martian base has been established. The player is an astronaut on a Marswalk who visits labeled landmarks and science stops, responds to hazard warnings, and monitors a suit status display. It answers the "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map" challenge by turning NASA data into an immersive map that helps people understand a location before a real Marswalk, with astronaut safety at the center. A first-person view shows distance, scale, and terrain better than a flat map, so crews and the public can build intuition for Mars surface conditions.
details:
How it works

The player spawns near a mission base on the Jezero terrain and walks under Mars-like gravity (3.71 m/s²). Labeled stops mark three Vallis landmarks, three craters, the Perseverance and Ingenuity landing spots, a current-location marker, Mars base marker and three science-fact stops. Hazard markers show warnings when the player enters a danger area. A suit HUD shows depleting oxygen and battery, a slightly varying suit temperature, suit pressure, external pressure, and radiation level.

Benefits and intended impact

It shows near-real terrain shape and scale from an astronaut's eye level.

It puts location and safety information in one view.

It needs no technical skill, so students, planners, and the public can use it.

It aims to show how NASA data can become an engaging, safety-first exploration tool, and it's a base for future mission-planning layers.

Tools and hardware

Software: Unreal Engine 5.8, Blender 5.2, NASA JPL Mars Trek, Visual Studio, Windows Game Bar, Clipchamp

Programming: Unreal Blueprint visual scripting (no traditional code)

Hardware: HP Victus laptop, Intel Core i7 (13th gen), NVIDIA RTX 4050, 24 GB RAM

NASA data: Mars Trek Jezero Crater export (topographic elevation and optical imagery), plus NASA Perseverance and Ingenuity 3D models

Other assets: Sketchfab models (landing pod, Mars base, rock)

Creativity

Most Mars maps are flat screens. This one puts the user on the surface as an astronaut and uses game mechanics (depleting oxygen, hazard warnings, low gravity) to make safety information feel real.

Factors considered

Safety: consumables, suit conditions, radiation, and terrain hazards

Honest realism: gravity matches Mars. Temperature, pressure, and radiation values are simulated, based on published figures (external pressure of about 0.8 kPa from Perseverance MEDA measurements, suit pressure of about 29.6 kPa from NASA suit specifications).

Performance: a detailed terrain tuned to run smoothly on a laptop

Access: a downloadable Windows build plus a demo video

Scope: built within the event, so it uses two data types

Limits and future work

The map currently uses two NASA data types (topographic and optical). Future versions would add mineral and slope layers, switchable layers, and a marked route with distances.

The Terrain is set to X: 778 m, Y: 778 m, Z: 108 m (resized in blender) with reduced texture resolution for better performance.

Use of AI

The AI chatbot Claude (from Anthropic) was used as a learning and troubleshooting assistant for Unreal Engine. The scene, terrain, interface, and implementation were built by the developer. No AI image or 3D generators produced the final assets.

Team

Ayush Debnath: the sole developer (idea, design, modeling, scene setup, Unreal implementation, video)
